name: Benguela Current
scope: Specified northward shelf-edge Benguela regional reference branch from an offshore Cape Agulhas regional gate to the nominal 15 degrees S Angola–Benguela front region. Excludes broad offshore Benguela extensions, Agulhas ring paths, southward undercurrent and the entire upwelling-ecosystem perimeter. Gate coordinates are OSW regional approximations; no continuous measured shelf-edge axis is inferred.
layer: Northward shelf-edge branch reference geography; no fixed velocity layer diagnosed. Distinct from offshore/underlying circulation.
time_convention: General editorial reference sketch; combines regional source descriptions, not a simultaneous 1997 or decadal inverse-model current axis.
source_locator: Section 3.1.3: eastern boundary Benguela system and Cape Agulhas region; distinguish sampled sections from whole-path geography. Shelf-edge northern convention uses Lass et al. (2000), Introduction: cold northward shelf-edge current and Angola–Benguela confluence near 15 degrees S; observed front at 16.5 degrees S in the April–May 1997 survey.
source_citation: Caínzos et al. (2023), Consistent picture of the horizontal circulation of the Atlantic Ocean over 3 decades, Ocean Science 19, 1009–1045.
source_license: Factual geographic references only; no source prose, figures, provider geometry or model data packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse regional offshore waypoints. Sources define flow identity and broad endpoint geography, not these intermediate vertices or longitudes. The path is not a digitized source curve, observed axis, bathymetric contour or diagnosed velocity field.
scenario_rule: Three uniform longitude shifts (-0.25/0/+0.25 degrees) crossed with independent endpoint latitude shifts (-0.5/0/+0.5 degrees): 54 editorial scenarios across two northern-gate conventions. No empirical positional error implied. The 1997 observed front at 16.5 degrees S is retained as a separate source-specific alternative route rather than treated as the universal front location.
remaining_gates: Independent review of source-specific start/end conventions, branches and seasonal endpoint alternatives.
Check offshore waypoints against reproducible shelf/slope or velocity geometry at suitable resolution.
Canonical claim, geometry and measurement integration before public admission.
figure_source_label: Caínzos et al. (2023); Lass et al. (2000)

supporting_sources.citation: Lass, Schmidt, Mohrholz and Nausch (2000), Hydrographic and Current Measurements in the Area of the Angola–Benguela Front, Journal of Physical Oceanography 30, 2589–2609.
supporting_sources.locator: Introduction (northward shelf-edge flow and confluence near 15 degrees S); abstract (front observed at 16.5 degrees S during April–May 1997).
supporting_sources.role: Source-specific northern branch/front convention; not an entire-current survey.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Alternative northern gate using the source’s April–May 1997 front latitude; this sketch is not an observed 1997 whole-current path.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 54 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
